# New renderings — iliad-081 (13.361–454)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὃ δ’ ἐπεύξατο φώνησέν τε (13.373, half-line speech introduction) | "and he vaunted and spoke:" | "and Idomeneus cried out in triumph over him, and spoke:" | "and he prayed", "boasted and said", "and made his vow"; ἐπεύχομαι of a taunt keeps "vaunts" / "cries out in triumph" (table 5.119, 10.368, 11.431), φωνέω "speak" |
| Δηΐφοβος / Ἰδομενεὺς δ’ ἔκπαγλον ἐπεύξατο μακρὸν ἀΰσας (13.413 = 13.445 with the name changed; whole-line speech introduction) | "And Deiphobus / Idomeneus terribly vaunted, shouting loudly:" | "And Deiphobus / Idomeneus cried out terribly in triumph, shouting loudly:" | "mightily", "terrifyingly" (ἐκπάγλως is "terribly" in the table, ἔκπαγλον here the adverbial accusative); μακρὸν ἀΰσας keeps "shouting loudly" (6.66) |
| ὣς ἔφατ’, Ἀργείοισι δ’ ἄχος γένετ’ εὐξαμένοιο (13.417, whole line) | "So he spoke, and for the Argives grief arose, as he declared it aloud," | "So he spoke, and grief came upon the Argives as he declared it aloud," | "as he boasted" (the table’s εὔχομαι of a non-prayer is "declare", 5.106, 8.198, 11.431), "as he vaunted" (kept for ἐπεύχομαι); ἄχος "grief" (table 2.171) |
| Ἀντίλοχος μεγαθύμου Νέστορος υἱός (13.400) | "Antilochus, son of great-hearted Nestor" | "Antilochus, son of great-hearted Nestor" | "Nestor’s son", "the son of Nestor the great-souled"; μεγάθυμος keeps "great-hearted" (table 1.123) |
| μενεχάρμης Ἀντίλοχος (13.396; the table’s μενεχάρμαι of the Aetolians, 9.529) | "Antilochus, steadfast in the fray" | "Antilochus, steadfast in the fray" | "staunch in battle", "stout in fight"; applied to a single man with no change |
| ἥρως Ἰδομενεύς (13.384, 13.439) | "the hero Idomeneus" | "the hero Idomeneus" | "warrior", "lord"; ἥρως "hero" (table 11.771) |
| δουρὶ φαεινῷ (13.370, 13.403) | "with his shining spear" | "his shining spear" | "bright", "gleaming" (reserved for γλαυκῶπις), "polished"; φαεινός "shining" (table 5.215) |
| διοτρεφής (Αἰσυήταο διοτρεφέος, 13.427; genitive) | "Zeus-nurtured" | "Zeus-nurtured" | "Zeus-reared", "nurtured by Zeus", "noble"; follows the table’s vocative διοτρεφές "Zeus-nurtured one" |
| ἐΐσκω with the infinitive (ἐΐσκομεν ἄξιον εἶναι, 13.446) | "deem" | "reckon" | "liken" (the table’s ἐΐσκω "liken", 5.181 and 13.313, is the transitive "compare" and does not fit "we … to be worth something"), "guess"; the note says it is the verb that elsewhere means "liken" |
| καρφαλέον … ἄϋσεν (of a shield, 13.409) · αὖον ἄϋσεν (of a man, 13.441) | "dry … rang" · "dry he cried out" | "rang harshly" · "cried out harshly" | "rattled", "hollowly"; follows the table’s αὖον ἀΰτευν "rang dry" / "rang harshly" (12.160), with ἀΰω of a person "cry out" and of a thing "ring"; both are said to be the same dry sound in the notes |
| φορέεσκε (of a breastplate, 13.372 = 13.398) | "kept carrying" | "wore" | "carried" in `i` (the table’s φορέω "carry"; the table’s avoided "wear" at 4.143 decides an object that is not known, but here the object is a breastplate, so "wore" is safe); `l` keeps "kept carrying" (table 2.770) |
| ἀλλ’ ὃ μὲν ἄντα ἰδὼν ἠλεύατο χάλκεον ἔγχος (13.404; = 13.184 with the next words changed) | "But he, looking straight at it, avoided the bronze spear" | "But Idomeneus, seeing it coming straight at him, avoided the bronze spear;" | the published `i` names Teucer, and the subject is Idomeneus here, so the name is changed and nothing else; "though only just" is dropped with τυτθόν, which this unit does not have |
| ἐάλη (πᾶς ἐάλη, 13.408; aorist passive of εἴλω) | "was hemmed in" | "crouched" | "was huddled", "cowered" (decide more than the verb says); `l` keeps the table’s εἴλω "hem in" (1.409, 11.413), `i` gives the posture the shield-picture needs |
| ἀτρέμας ἑσταότα (13.438) · ἑσταότα | "standing motionless" | "stood motionless" | "stock still", "rooted"; ἀτρέμας "motionless" (table 5.523, 13.280) |

One-off rare words (μεσαιπόλιος, ἀχερωΐς, βλωθρή, νεήκης, ὑψιπέτηλος, κανών, ἐεδνωταί, οὐρίαχος, πυλάρτης) are rendered in the units and discussed in the notes only; none is likely to recur as a formula.
